en_id.challenge.g1_c1.prompt: How Indonesians often ask “how are you?” (casual).
en_id.challenge.g1_c3.prompt: Thanks (very casual, with a soft particle).
en_id.challenge.g2_c1.prompt: Nice to meet you — I'm Budi (casual connective).
en_id.challenge.g2_c4.prompt: What are you up to right now? (casual ask)
en_id.challenge.g2_c4.note: Very common in Jabodetabek small talk.
en_id.challenge.n1_c4.prompt: One thousand (one word learners often need in shops).
en_id.challenge.n1_c5.prompt: It's one thousand five hundred, yeah? (colloquial price line)
en_id.challenge.d1_c1.prompt: I'm so hungry right now (casual, with intensifier).
en_id.challenge.d1_c4.prompt: Where do we want to eat? (casual invite)
en_id.challenge.p1_c1.prompt: Have you eaten yet? (with the soft tag particle)
en_id.challenge.p1_c2.prompt: What time is the pickup? (tag particle at end)
en_id.challenge.p1_c3.prompt: Traffic was awful earlier (nih for empathy).
en_id.challenge.p1_c4.prompt: Fine, let's just go for it (casual 'gas').
en_id.feature.daily_smalltalk: Small talk in Jakarta casual often stacks short clauses; don't translate word-for-word from English politeness.
en_id.feature.particles_nih: 'Nih' tags the sentence like 'here / you know'—keep it at the end unless you're echoing a native clip.
